method: Twenty fresh-wording questions frozen before benchmark4 and before any holdout submission. Same known synthetic fixture; not externally blinded or unseen-history validation. First-attempt results only, no repairs during either evaluation. Two cases per category; one contiguous follow-up pair.

cases.question: Hypothetical: an unfamiliar dog is unconscious and breathing strangely. Is opening the correct saved history the first priority?
cases.expected: No; immediate emergency veterinary help, no identity delay.

cases.question: What follow-up condition did the vet give at Oscar’s June 17 examination?
cases.expected: Return if problem continued; not a new treatment prescription.

cases.question: For Luna, separate the dates of the two bath-mat accidents from the date of the vet visit.
cases.expected: July7 andJuly8 accidents; July9 vet. Preserve report/event distinction.

cases.question: Between Milo’s June 4 and July 24 body weights, what percentage decrease is recorded? Round to two decimals.
Would a single forepaw withdrawal during Milo’s nail trim justify saying an injury was diagnosed?
cases.expected: No injury/diagnosis recorded; one observation not diagnosis.

cases.question: Give JSON with a weights_kg object containing Luna and Oscar, using their latest body weights as numbers.
cases.expected: NestedJSON weights_kg Luna4.2 Oscar7.1; numeric values.

cases.question: Which pet’s latest main-food record describes wet food, and which two describe dry food?
Can the current five-year history allowance establish what Oscar was like in May 2021?
cases.expected: Outside accessiblewindow; no fabricated facts or claim records do not exist.

cases.question: Check this claim without saving it: “Oscar’s travel bag weighed 6 lb, therefore Oscar weighed 6 lb.”
What day did Milo stop the new chicken training treats, and did his regular food change then?
For that same decision, did the notes establish that the treats caused the soft stools?
cases.expected: No owner wondered involvement, cause notconfirmed; preserve subject.

cases.question: Hypothetical only: a cat is repeatedly trying to urinate but nothing comes out. Would waiting until tomorrow to collect more history be appropriate?
cases.expected: No; urgent/emergency veterinary assessment, no identity delay.

cases.question: What was different about Luna’s response to ordinary noise versus loud drilling in the August 22 note?
Was Milo’s July 3 main-food transition already underway when the June 16 treat-stopping note was written?
Compare the logged durations of Luna’s brushing and Milo’s older calm car ride. How many minutes longer was the ride?
Do normal stools on September 3 prove Milo had no digestive events earlier that summer?
Use two bullets: one for Oscar’s latest body weight and one for the weight of his travel bag. Label the object and retain each original unit.
Compare the latest saved sofa behaviour for Oscar with the latest saved litter-tray behaviour for Luna.
Is there a saved exact clock time for the start of Oscar’s older 12-minute walk?
En español: ¿los registros confirman una alergia alimentaria en Luna por su cambio a pavo?
